problem: VLN instructions often mention landmarks the agent's visual encoder cannot recognize (relying on the instructor's prior knowledge, e.g. sofa -> living room) or landmarks that fit multiple candidate viewpoints (e.g. 'the door'), so fine-grained grounding is ineffective.
motivation: Instructors and agents have different visual abilities, and the small VLN datasets do not let the agent learn the instructor's prior knowledge. Converting the instruction at each step into a representation based on recognizable and distinctive landmarks should ease grounding and improve generalization to unseen environments.
key_idea: Add a translator module to a VLN agent that, at each step, turns the full instruction plus current candidate views into a sub-instruction representation focused on recognizable and distinctive landmarks, pre-trained on a CLIP-built synthetic sub-instruction dataset (SyFiS) with generation and contrastive tasks.
insight: Grounding improves when the instruction is re-expressed in terms of what the agent can see and what separates the target from the other candidates. Ablations show SIG and DSL pre-training each incrementally raise unseen SPL (R2R baseline 0.611 -> 0.623 -> 0.627), and the Sub-instruction Split (SS) task helps on R2R (unseen SR 0.690) but hurts on R2R-Last, which has only one sub-instruction to learn from. Adding SyFiS to agent pre-training also helps (row 11 -> 12), so the synthetic data is useful in itself. The qualitative analysis shows the translator learns landmark associations, e.g. cupboard -> kitchen, but inherits SyFiS data biases, e.g. oven vs countertop.
method: SyFiS synthetic dataset: for each viewpoint of R2R and PREVALENT trajectories (1,076,818 in total), builds template sub-instructions of the form motion indicator + landmark. The motion verb comes from a dictionary of 6 categories chosen by heading/elevation difference (threshold 30°). Landmarks are top-k CLIP zero-shot object labels, and the distinctive ones appear only in the target view.

Contrastive positives/negatives: the positive sub-instruction contains a distinctive landmark; easy negatives use landmarks seen only in non-target candidates; hard negatives use non-distinctive landmarks seen in both target and other candidates. This gives 1 positive and 3 negatives per viewpoint.

Translator architecture: a Speaker-like module with LSTM encoders for text and candidate-view features, soft attention from text over views, and an MLP output over the vocabulary. It runs at every step, not on the whole trajectory offline.

Pre-training tasks: Sub-instruction Generation (SIG, cross-entropy against the positive sub-instruction) and Distinctive Sub-instruction Learning (DSL, triplet loss with an anchor made by swapping the motion verb within its category). The total loss is a1*SIG + a2*DSL with a1=a2=1.
Integration into VLN-BERT: the translator produces the translated sub-instruction representation X~' and an MLP attention mask X_m'. The agent's text input becomes [X; X~'; X_m' ⊙ X].

Navigation training: IL + RL mixture (lambda=0.2) with auxiliary SIG loss and the Sub-instruction Split (SS) BCE loss on the attention mask, using FG-R2R/SyFiS alignments. Weights are beta = 1, 1, 0.1. Inference is greedy.
Agent pre-training: extra RxR and Marky-mT5 data (the '+' variant), plus SyFiS ('++'), following LOViS.

setting.backbone: VLN-BERT (recurrent cross-modal Transformer) + LSTM translator, ResNet-152 (Places365) visual features, BERT text init; trained
setting.training_data: R2R + PREVALENT augmented data; extra pre-training with RxR and Marky-mT5; SyFiS (~1.08M trajectories, 5-7 viewpoints each, 1 positive + 3 negatives per viewpoint); FG-R2R alignments for the FG variant
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views), candidate viewpoint features, ResNet-152 Places365
setting.privileged: none at test time (training uses FG-R2R human alignments/SyFiS synthetic alignments)

numbers.extra: extra pre-training RxR + Marky-mT5 + SyFiS; trained on R2R + PREVALENT; translator not optimized during navigation training
trained with FG-R2R and SyFiS alignments; translator optimized with SIG+SS; extra pre-training data

numbers_note: Metrics are printed as fractions (e.g. 0.67) and converted to percentages; NE, CLS and sDTW converted likewise (R4R). The ablation table gives finer variants, e.g. R2R val-unseen SR 0.690 / SPL 0.633 with SIG+DSL+SS.
results: VLN-Trans-FG-R2R reaches R2R val-unseen SR 69 / SPL 63 and test-unseen SR 66 / SPL 60, beating HAMT (ViT) (66 / 61 val-unseen) and LOViS (65 / 59) despite using only ResNet features. It also improves on R4R val-unseen (SR 46, sDTW 25 vs LOViS 45 / 23), and on R2R-Last raises unseen SR to 50 from HAMT's 45.
limitations: The translator outputs only a latent representation, not an actual instruction, which reduces interpretability.
Only ResNet visual features are used; ViT/CLIP features are untested.
It is evaluated only in simulation; the translator inherits biases from the CLIP-derived SyFiS landmark statistics, leading to wrong landmark associations (e.g. oven vs countertop).
